newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KNPC targets rise in refinery capacity - report.
newsitem.headline: KNPC targets rise in refinery capacity - report.

text.p: State oil refiner Kuwait National Petroleum Co (KNPC) wants to raise domestic refining capacity to one million barrels per day to prepare for a possible eventual rise in the country's OPEC output quota, a newspaper reported on Monday.
"With (an anticipated) increase in the OPEC quota the target would...be one million refined barrels per day," al-Anba quoted Abdul-Rahman al-Taweel, KNPC's deputy managing director, as saying.
Taweel did not give a timeframe for the capacity increase.
"The strategy of the Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC)...includes an increase in refining capacity of the Kuwaiti refineries in line with the expected rise in crude oil production," he added.
KNPC is the refining arm of state-owned KPC, which oversees the country's oil industry.
Kuwait's current crude oil production quota stands at two million barrels per day.
The Gulf Arab state has said it wants an increase of about 200,000 barrels per day in its quota when OPEC considers a rise in its 25.033 million barrels per day output ceiling.
OPEC has kept quotas frozen for all members but Iraq since September 1993 in a bid to prop up prices.
KNPC wants to increase its domestic capacity to 900,000 bpd at the beginning of 1998, said Taweel. KNPC's capacity stood at 895,000 bpd in February.
